step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify the external actors: 'CALLER CARRIE' represented as end-user (UserConsumerMobile) and 'AGENT ANDY' represented as internal agent staff (UserCompanyDeveloper). External CRM systems are mapped to ThirdParty.
2. Identify AWS services drawn on the whiteboard:
   - Connect (Amazon Connect for chat/voice handling)
   - Lambda (top row for IVR contact flow logic)
   - ECS (Elastic Container Service running microservices for CRM integration)
   - SES (Simple Email Service for email ingestion)
   - Lambda (bottom row for email processing logic)
   - DynamoDB (for storing email/chat state data)
   - EC2 (representing ContactSuite core application hosting ELB/EC2/ASG)
   - RDS (relational database backend for ContactSuite)
3. Map data flows:
   - Flow 0: Caller Carrie -> Connect -> Lambda -> ECS -> ThirdParty (CRMs).
   - Flow 1: Caller Carrie -> SES -> Lambda -> DynamoDB.
   - Flow 2: Agent Andy -> ContactSuite (EC2) -> RDS.

graph.name: ContactSuite Contact Center Architecture
graph.notes: ContactSuite leverages Amazon Connect, ECS microservices, SES, Lambda, DynamoDB, and RDS to build an agile contact center platform.
